A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same V-VAE study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered content can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning evaluations on HumanChatBench and DialogBench, component ablations, structured-persona comparisons and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds evaluations of three additional backbone configurations in Appendix A.4 and Table 6.

M1.justification: The fixed LLM persona extractor, three-axis latent space, empirical-prior sampling and reconstruction objective remain unchanged. The Table 3 row relabeling and corrected prior-support definition do not establish an altered implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use HumanChatData, HumanChatBench and the same seven DialogBench tasks. Table 6 adds model configurations, while Appendix A.3 describes the existing annotators rather than establishing a changed population or dataset.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds FT and P+FT comparator results for DS-7B-base, DS-7B-chat and chatglm3-6B alongside their SP+FT variants. This extends the model-specific comparisons; the comparison strategies and commercial-model comparator set remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 introduces evaluations using DS-7B-base, DS-7B-chat and chatglm3-6B, extending backbone and model-size settings. The existing dataset splits, metrics, component-ablation design and zero/2/5-shot evaluations are retained.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 3, structured-versus-unstructured comparison in Table 5 and qualitative case in Figure 4 are retained. Table 6 supplies additional standard benchmark evaluations without a distinct new ablation, robustness protocol or error analysis.

E5.justification: Model performance remains reported as point scores, without added run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-test procedures. The new age summary in Appendix A.3 describes the annotator cohort rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 6 substantially expands the results with full three-strategy evaluations on three additional backbones. The findings are mixed: chatglm3-6B FT exceeds SP+FT on six of seven DialogBench tasks. Tables 2–5 retain their numerical values. Section 4.5 also removes a numerical example incorrectly attributing StepAI's 84.08 CP and 88.66 EC scores to GPT-4o-mini.

T1.justification: Equation 7 changes from asserting that the constructed feature set is nonempty to explicitly requiring extracted values to be non-null inside the set definition. This corrects the mathematical specification of prior support; the variational objective and Appendix A.1 derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about dynamic fine-grained persona control, HumanChatData/HumanChatBench and superior performance. The introductory claim of a 7.2% improvement over Qwen-7B is also unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a specific sociocultural generalizability limitation for the homogeneous university annotator cohort and explains the intended mitigation through diverse hometowns. Section 2.2 adds an interpretation linking human–LLM communication differences to the chosen latent axes; the existing results discussion and limitations otherwise remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 replaces the future dataset-release pledge with a HumanChatData access link and a statement that the platform has been de-anonymized. Appendix A.3 newly documents recruitment, native language, age and geographic background. Existing prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 replaces the role-play and persona-simulation survey with a sociolinguistic account of human-likeness. Numerous earlier references are removed, while works including Danesi, Schneider, Reinhart and Altenburger are introduced to ground the latent-space design, substantially changing its research positioning.

P1.justification: Section 2.2 is rewritten and retitled, author affiliations and contact information change, and acknowledgments plus two appendix subsections are added. Table 3 standardizes the Qwen variant's name to SP+FT. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 6, moves Figures 1 and 2 earlier, and rearranges the appendix case and prompt figures. Existing figure content and table designs are largely preserved; these are localized additions and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through dataset access information, specific annotator demographics and generalizability qualifications, while Table 6 broadens the empirical evidence. It also corrects the prior-support definition and removes a misattributed numerical example. The gains are limited because the added DialogBench results are mixed, yet Appendix A.4 simply asserts consistency with the unchanged main conclusions.
